messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the k8s rebuild we're seeing steady KV cache memory growth on checkout workloads. Profiling points to cross-request reuse of long prefixes leaking small fragments.

maya: sample trace: evict loop shows 1500 allocations/min, 230MB/hr growth on node-3, hit rate steady but residency fragmented.

maya: example keying scheme we're using:
```
kv_key = tenant_id + ':' + prefix_hash + (session_id ? ':S' + session_id : '')
```
This seems to create many near-duplicate keys when sessions rotate mid-request.

raj: @maya do we have a flamegraph or pager output? is this longctx-specific ( > 4k tokens)?

maya: yes longctx heavy — most growth happens when seq_len > 2k. Flamegraph attached (summary): heap dominated by slab fragments from 64B-512B buckets.

sam: hypothesis: session_id in key prevents reuse across requests for same prefix. Can we try tenant-salted prefix + TTL-based sticky hint instead? e.g. drop session_id for prefix-only keys and keep session pin for KV handles.

emily: any perf tradeoffs? batching might coalesce better if keys are normalized.

maya: initial microbench: removing session_id from prefix keys increased reuse by 18% and reduced eviction rate 2.4x, but introduced correctness concerns for multi-conversation users in private deploys.

evict-bot: [alert] node-3 eviction spikes: 2026-06-12T03:21:44Z, evicted_pages=1243, fragmentation=0.32

sam: proposed plan:
1) A/B: normalize prefix keys (tenant + prefix_hash only) for 10% traffic
2) Add sticky-hint header per-connection to prefer local cache
3) Monitor eviction rate and correctness via canary prompt set

raj: +1. add a regression test for cross-session bleed (sample prompts) and a metric for 'prefix-reuse-hit'

maya: I'll open PR with keying change + canary config. tagging @emily for batching impact metric. :thumbsup:

emily: ack, will add coalescing histograms and cost delta dashboard.

maya: thanks — will post PR link when ready.
